display_name: Aufenthaltsverordnung (Residence Regulation), § 26 and Anlage C: the airport transit visa, with the power it rests on (Aufenthaltsgesetz § 99(3a)) and the citation requirement of Grundgesetz Art. 80(1) sentence 3
citation: Aufenthaltsverordnung vom 25. November 2004 (BGBl. I S. 2945), zuletzt geändert durch Art. 12 Abs. 9 G v. 22.10.2026 (BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 318) (the site's 'Stand' line on 2026-11-02), § 26 and Anlage C only
authority: Federal Republic of Germany. § 99(3a) AufenthG authorises the Federal Ministry of the Interior, in agreement with the Foreign Office and without the Bundesrat's consent, to name the states whose nationals need an airport transit visa.

source.provider: gesetze-im-internet.de (Bundesamt für Justiz, run by juris GmbH)
source.note: Per-norm pages for AufenthV § 26, Anlage C and AufenthG § 99, converted to one line per paragraph. The 2015 amending regulation (BGBl. 2015 I S. 2467) could not be obtained from the gazette; its preamble is deposited only as the German quotation in the article, labelled an aid. The EU Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009) was not deposited: EUR-Lex answered the consolidated text with HTTP 202 and an empty body (not retried or worked around).

why_this_subject: Felix Ringe and Linus Folkerts, 'Legal exploits may emerge at scale' (28 October 2026), https://www.felixringe.com/legal-exploits/, Case 2: they argue that the 2015 addition of Mali (and South Sudan) to Anlage C is void because the amending regulation's preamble does not cite § 99(3a) AufenthG, the power to name the states. This subject encodes the rule as printed, the power it needs, and the citation test, and answers the traveller's question under both readings. It does not decide which reading is right.
encodings_note: One row. It encodes § 26 and Anlage C of the Aufenthaltsverordnung only, not the Regulation; read the display_name as the subject, not as a claim about the encoding's coverage.
